prompt: This research notebook studies numerical algorithms. A library stores books in numbered rooms. Room one contains astronomy, room two mathematics, and room three history. An accurate answer must distinguish an approximate candidate set from the selected set. Explain why removing an incorrect candidate can change a normalized weighted average.
scope: Dense greedy Qwen3 generation is unchanged. The external Quest-style key min/max bound ranks complete blocks.
These rankings do not evaluate FlashNext's learned QSA selector or a deployed predictor. No latency or model-quality measurements.

Query heads align by index across dense Qwen3 layers as a proxy. FlashNext QSA shares one selection across heads and occurs every fourth layer; the immediately preceding dense layer here is a different source.
Step zero initializes temporal history. The current target ranking is used only as the comparison set.

policies.rank: Descending fused selector score, with ascending block ID to break exact score ties.
policies.temporal: Previous decode step's ranking from the same layer, truncated to the budget.
policies.layer: Current decode step's ranking from the immediately preceding layer, truncated to the budget.
policies.interleave: Alternating unique admissions from temporal then preceding-layer ranking. Each source advances past duplicates in its own ranking. No target-driven fill.
policies.source_comparison: Intersection and unique hits compare the two individually truncated predictions at equal budget.
policies.target_rank_quartile_retention: Fraction of each current target rank quartile found in the budgeted prediction.
policies.source_rank_quartile_retention: Fraction of each complete source ranking quartile found in the current target; independent of the prediction budget.
